philosophy for all times and places Paul is being practical and Paul is trying to avoid getting Christians into trouble
before the escaton Paul thought the end of days was going to be any moment all of Paul's genuine writings reflect this
idea that the time is short the form of this world is passing away and we need to act in accordance with that so here's
EP Sanders one of the most authoritative Scholars of Paul in the world on this passage as I remarked before Paul's
radical theology neither Jew nor Greek neither free nor slave neither male nor female could potentially have very profound social results but prior to the
escaton he did not want his churches to disturb the social order to this degree his support of judicial and political
Authority fits into his eschatological thinking while Christians awaited the return of the Lord they should not attempt to change the status quo by for
example campaigning for the freedom of slaves and opposing unjust laws and rulers and then here is commentary from
Robert jwt's hermana commentary on Romans Romans 13 1-7 was not intended to create the foundation of a political
ethic for all times and places in succeeding Generations a task for which it has proven to be singularly ill suited believing himself to be a member
of the end time generation Paul had no interest in the concerns that would later burden Christian ethics and which continue to dominate the exegetical discussion his goal was to appeal to the
Roman audience as he conceived it addressing their concerns in a manner that fit the occasion of his forthcoming visit so just like Christians today who
think we don't have to worry about climate change because God's going to fix everything Paul is just saying don't
overturn the social apple cart because everything's going to end soon anyway and we don't want to cause unnecessary
trouble for ourselves this is why Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7 stay in whatever circumstances you were when God called
you the time is short the form of this world is passing away Paul's rhetoric in Romans 13:1 has absolutely nothing
whatsoever to do with any time period Beyond Paul's own day too many people read the Bible not to understand what
the authors wanted to communicate but because they want to use it as a tool for structuring power and value values to serve their own interests and the
interests of their identity politics
